title: What does the US president do?

scenes.narration: One person runs the most powerful office on Earth. So what does the US president actually do all day?
scenes.visual: The White House, with the question popping up over it.

scenes.narration: Article Two of the Constitution gives the job three big hats: head of state, head of government, and commander in chief.
scenes.visual: Three hats appearing one after another.

scenes.narration: Congress writes the laws, but the president can sign them or veto them. Congress needs a two-thirds vote to override.
scenes.visual: A pen signing a bill, then a big veto stamp.

scenes.narration: The president also runs the executive branch, picking cabinet members, ambassadors and federal judges. Many need Senate approval.
scenes.visual: An org chart filling in with appointees.

scenes.narration: On the world stage, the president leads diplomacy and negotiates treaties, which the Senate must ratify.
scenes.visual: A globe with handshake lines between countries.

scenes.narration: To get the job, you must be thirty five, a natural born citizen, and live in the US for fourteen years. A term lasts four years, with a limit of two.
scenes.visual: A checklist of requirements, then a calendar showing the term.

scenes.narration: Big power, but it's checked by Congress and the courts. The president leads, but never alone.
scenes.visual: Three pillars balancing on a scale, ending on the takeaway line.
